proposal:
STATUS: nothing executed; hand derivations from the supplied code; literature (Fredman-Khachiyan 1996, Eiter-Gottlob 1995) cited from memory. No polynomial-SAT claim.

A. AUDIT (new items)
1. `step` is cached on the raw tuple `tuple(restrict(...))`, while `refute` runs on the canonical `reduced`. Different raw tuples with one canonical form miss the cache. That matches the trusted 4-of-12 repeated IALH inputs; memoising `refute` on `reduced` changes no status.
2. `elim` can destroy clause purity. On Maj9 (section E) eliminating variable 1 is accepted (252 to 182 clauses) and creates 70 mixed width-8 resolvents. A purity-based engine must run before `elim_plus`.
3. Reconfirmed: `_verify_certificate` builds blocks from every original clause; `probe` returns UNSAT only after the subset check, a verified compression and 2-SAT failure.

B. OBSERVATION
The Neon58 quotient and the peer Neon96 fixture are the same kind of object. Both are pure (every clause all-positive or all-negative) and intersecting (every positive clause shares a variable with every negative clause). Hand-checked on Neon96: negative clauses are vertex covers of C5+C5 or of C6, positive clauses are edge unions, so none of the 60x30 pairs is disjoint. Neon58 quotient, from the brief's description: none of 16x32.

C. SOUND RESTRICTED RULE: DUAL-DPLL
Recognition. Renamable purity is GF(2)-linear: literals in one clause must agree in sign after flipping, which is a parity union-find in near-linear time. The disjointness graph D joins variable-disjoint positive/negative clause pairs: |P||N| mask tests.
Lemma 1 (closure). Restriction never makes an intersecting pair disjoint: if the shared variable is set true the positive clause is deleted; if false, the negative one. So D only shrinks under branching and unit propagation.
Lemma 2 (bound, D empty). If the sum of 2^-|C| is below 1, a model exists and conditional expectations finds it (verified by evaluation). Otherwise the shortest clause C has width at most log2 m, and every opposite clause meets it, so some variable x of C occurs in at least a 1/log2 m fraction of the opposite side. Branching on x satisfies that fraction on one branch and deletes C on the other. With v=|P||N| after subsumption, T(v) <= T((1-1/log2 m)v) + T(v-1) + 1, hence m^O(log^2 m) nodes. This is Fredman-Khachiyan algorithm A read as DPLL: its decomposition is Shannon expansion and its absorption is the existing `canon` subsumption. Quasi-polynomial, not polynomial.
Soundness needs nothing new. Any branching order is sound, so there is no certificate object; only the bound uses the lemma.
Lemma 3 (arbitrary extras; claimed, needs independent proof). Fix a renaming. Let c = (mixed clauses) + nu(D), where nu is maximum matching = minimum clause cover (Koenig; Hopcroft-Karp). Branch first-true-literal on each mixed or cover clause: at most w^c leaves, each pure and intersecting by Lemma 1. Total nodes <= w^c * m^O(log^2 m). Each extra clause costs a factor of at most its width; none voids the method.
Bit cost per node: subsumption O(m^2 w) literal comparisons on log n-bit ids; leaf test on dyadic rationals of w+log m bits.
Work invariant to instrument: v strictly decreases on both branches, by the factor above on one.

D. NEON58
Pipeline: existing exact compression (Lean proof unchanged), recognition gives c=0, then DUAL-DPLL. Hand trace with units kept on the trail: residuals form a chain F(p,q) of full-pair counts, one singleton state per link, and one-sided tails closed by unit propagation. That is O(k^2) memoised states, at most 64 for k=4, each no larger than the input: polynomial in L = Theta(k 2^k) for this family only.

E. PREDICTIONS (engine unimplemented; independent test)
T1 Neon58 quotient: c=0, UNSAT, at most 64 memoised states, zero HNF calls.
T2 Neon96: c=0, UNSAT, zero HNF calls. State count not traced.
T3 Maj9 stress (9 variables; every 5-subset as a positive and as a negative clause; 252 clauses): pinned root IALH returns UNKNOWN with 126 windows, 4032 tuples, 0 rows (each table is the 20 weight-2/3 tuples, a full lattice). Pinned peak not predicted. DUAL-DPLL: the residual depends only on the true/false counts, at most 55 states.
T4 control, pigeonhole 5 into 4: pure, nu(D)=5, bound 4^5 leaves, no gain; must fall back.
T5 fixture Maj7: compression skipped `incompatible_greedy_basis` (basis x1+xj; block {2,3,4,5} gets none), core `no_clauses_removed`, 35 four-windows give tables of six weight-2 tuples, then window [1,2,3,4,5] is empty: UNSAT, peak 0, 36 windows, 592 tuples.

F. LIMITS
The 20-variable Neon58 input is not renamable-pure: [5,8,13,14,19,20] and [5,8,-13,-14,19,20] give contradictory parities. The repair therefore depends on compression succeeding. An extra clause that blocks compression leaves dozens of mixed clauses, and Lemma 3 is useless there.
missing_theorem:
Two gaps, stated separately.
MT1 (precise, plausibly provable). For every CNF with m clauses and any renaming with deficiency c there is a branching rule giving at most (log2 m)^O(c) * m^O(log^2 m) nodes, replacing w^c. Known pieces: if the shortest clause lies in a minimum cover, first-true branching on it lowers c at branching factor log2 m; if it lies outside and is D-adjacent to at most half the opposite side, one of its variables has opposite frequency at least 1/(2 log2 m) and Lemma 2's recurrence survives. Open corner: shortest clause outside every minimum cover and D-adjacent to more than half the opposite side (that side then has fewer than 2c clauses).
MT2 (the real obstruction, not claimed). Pure CNF with nonempty D is monotone SAT, which is NP-complete, and every CNF has c <= m. A bound polynomial in c for all inputs is P=NP. Even c=0 is hypergraph dualization, whose polynomial-time status is open. So the only all-work bounds here are quasi-polynomial at c=0 and w^c beyond. Also missing: choosing the renaming that minimises c (a signed-graph frustration problem; union-find finds a renaming only when zero mixed clauses is achievable).
self_attack:
1. Lemma 2 is literature. My contribution is identifying both live fixtures as dualization instances, the closure and extras lemmas, and the placement in this pipeline. Exponents are from memory.
2. The class is narrow. c=0 needs every opposite-sign pair to meet; random 3-CNF has c near m. For arbitrary SAT the bound is exponential. This is a restricted result.
3. T1's state count is a hand trace of one family under one tie-break. Pinned `canon` re-adds unit clauses, so an implementation reusing it may count differently.
4. To my recollection formula-caching DPLL is simulated by resolution; if that holds with subsumption-based memoisation, Haken's 2^Omega(h) pigeonhole bound applies to this engine (not to IALH). I have not checked that simulation.
5. Robustness to extras holds at quotient level only (section F). The original-input gap remains open.
6. The fixture is again an empty-table control and exercises no search. It only locates the boundary: window width+1 must fit k=5, which fails first at Maj9.
7. T3 and T5 assume unit propagation behaves as traced on one representative tuple per weight, and that SymPy HNF handles the rank-3 tables without incident.
8. Peak is not work: the memo table can hold as many states as there are nodes.
mechanism_signature: Pure-intersecting recognition (parity union-find renaming, clause disjointness graph D, Koenig deficiency c) feeding Fredman-Khachiyan dualization run as ordinary DPLL: shortest-clause max-frequency branching, subsumption, 2^-|C| counting leaf. No formula rewriting and no certificate. Literature bound m^O(log^2 m) at c=0; claimed factor w^c for arbitrary extras.
delta_from_prior: Round 89 (BVA), round 90 (bound-set quotient) and Fable73 (twin contraction) all rewrite the formula and need a certificate per rewrite. This proposal rewrites nothing: it is a branching rule plus a recognised class, sound by ordinary DPLL soundness. New: (1) Neon58 quotient and Neon96 identified as hypergraph-duality instances, giving one quasi-polynomial bound covering both, including the twin-free non-product Neon96; (2) closure Lemma 1 and a polynomial-time computable deficiency c pricing each extra clause at its width; (3) audit A1 (cache keyed before canonicalisation) and A2 (elim destroys purity); (4) stated limits: pigeonhole has c=h+1, dualization in P is open, the original 20-variable input is not renamable-pure.
